name: Posterior tibial tendon (PTTD)
goal: Settle the painful tendon on the inside of the ankle, then strengthen it step by step so it can hold up your arch again for walking, hiking and running.
whoFor: People diagnosed with early-stage posterior tibial tendon dysfunction: pain and sometimes swelling along the inside of the ankle, and the arch may be starting to drop.
notFor: A flat foot that has become rigid (no arch forms when you rise on tiptoe): see a foot and ankle specialist
Recent ankle surgery: follow your surgeon's protocol
trackedMetric: Pain on the inside of the ankle when walking or doing a heel raise (0-10)
painRules: Up to about 3 out of 10 during exercise is OK if it settles within 24 hours. If the ankle is more painful or swollen the next morning, drop back a step for a few days. Supportive shoes (or orthotics from your clinician) help while the tendon recovers.
redFlags: A sudden pop or tearing feeling, and you can't stand on tiptoe
The arch flattening noticeably over a few weeks
You can't do a single heel raise on that side at all
A lot of swelling, heat or redness
Numbness or tingling in the foot
If you have diabetes: a hot, swollen or changing-shape foot (see a doctor the same day)

phases.name: Calm and load gently
phases.entryCriteria: Pain on the inside of the ankle, worse with walking or running.
phases.exitCriteria: Walking is comfortable and the inversion holds cause little pain (2 out of 10 or less).

phases.name: Strengthen the tendon
phases.exitCriteria: 3 x 12 ball-squeeze heel raises with pain of 2 out of 10 or less, and no worse the next day.

items.note: Useful on sore days for pain relief.

phases.name: Build capacity, return to running
phases.exitCriteria: 20 or more single-leg heel raises without pain, and comfortable runs.

items.note: Keep your arch lifted as you lower.
Only once single-leg heel raises are pain-free: a step towards running.

references: Kulig K, et al. 2009. Nonsurgical management of posterior tibial tendon dysfunction with orthoses and resistive exercise: a randomized controlled trial. Phys Ther 89:26-37.
